docs.title: Project
docs.text:
Project registration establishes the high-level administrative umbrella for the data. A project can contain one or more related studies.

Testing Portal

Use the IMDA testing database for validation: https://ibdc.dbt.gov.in/imda_test/.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
Complete these checks before beginning a new submission:

  • Prepare raw and derived data files.
  • Compress complex raw data folders into individual ZIP archives before transfer.
  • Use only letters, numbers, hyphens, underscores, and dots in file names.
  • Do not use spaces or special characters in file names.
  • Organize raw data into clear local folders before compression.
  • Install an FTP client such as FileZilla.
  • Use open formats where possible. IMDA prefers mzML for MS data and nmrML for NMR data.
  • Collect name, email, and affiliation details for the Principal Investigator and all contributing authors.
  • Prepare the study summary, keywords, DOI where applicable, and ethical or institutional approval numbers.

docs.title: Access
docs.text: Option User Action Purpose User Registration Open User Registration. Creates the account required for data submission. Login Open Login. Starts an authenticated session for submission and dashboard access. Submit Click Submit after login. Opens the new data submission workflow.

docs.title: Register Project
docs.text: Purpose: Define the overall research initiative, funding source, and investigators responsible for the data.

docs.title: What to Fill
docs.text:
Field What to Enter Writing Guideline Title* Name of the overall research project, consortium, or data generation activity. Use one clear sentence or phrase. Project Contributors* Principal Investigator, submitter, and other responsible contributors. Enter full name, email, and institutional affiliation wherever requested. Research Area* Scientific domain of the project. Select the closest controlled term from the portal list. Funding Source* Grant agency, project number, institutional funding, or other support source. Use the official funder name and grant number if available. Project Description* Overall aim, biological context, and data type covered by the project. Keep it concise, usually 3-5 sentences.

Final Action:

  1. Fill all fields marked with an asterisk.
  2. Check the funding source carefully.
  3. Click Submit to generate the project identifier.

Project vs Study

The Project defines the who and why. The Study defines the specific experiment.

docs.title: Experiment
docs.text:
Experiment registration captures the analytical workflow and processed metabolite data.

Key Actions:

  • Select the analytical technique, such as MS or NMR.
  • Download and complete the appropriate experiment template.
  • Upload the analytical template and metabolite or compound file.
Template Category Example Columns Mandatory Rules Mass Spectrometry (MS) Mass Spectrometer Type, MS Instrument Name, MS Ionization Method, Acquisition Polarity Use dropdown lists where provided. Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) NMR Instrument Name, NMR Type, NMR Solvent Do not change column headers.

docs.title: What to Fill in the Experiment Template
docs.text: Column / Field Type What to Enter Writing Guideline Sample ID IMDA-generated sample ID from the Sample step. Copy exactly from the portal; do not use local sample names in this field. Assay / Technique MS or NMR assay used to generate the data. Use the portal dropdown term. Protocol / Method Details Sample preparation, extraction, chromatography, MS/NMR acquisition, and processing method details. Keep each method description short and factual, usually 2-4 lines. Instrument Name Official instrument model/name. Use the controlled term if available; otherwise request it through Update List. Ionization / Acquisition Polarity Ionization method and positive/negative polarity for MS data where applicable. Select from dropdowns; do not type variants manually if a controlled term exists. Raw Data File Name Exact uploaded ZIP or raw file name. Must match the FTP-uploaded file name exactly, including extension. MD5 Checksum 32-character checksum for the uploaded file. Use lowercase checksum values. Metabolite / Compound File Processed metabolite table with identifiers and quantified values. Include metabolite name, identifier, SMILES, InChI, and quantification data where available.

docs.title: Cross-Reference and Data Integrity
docs.text:
1. Retrieve sample IDs from Register Sample or My Sample and enter them in the template.
  2. Enter the MD5 checksum for each final zipped raw data file.
  3. Ensure the metabolite or compound file includes metabolite name, metabolite identifier, SMILES string, InChI ID, and quantification data where applicable.
  4. Match file names in the template exactly with files uploaded to the FTP server.
  5. Use NA for fields that are required but genuinely not applicable.

docs.title: FTP File Uploads
docs.text:
Use the FTP credentials provided by IMDA to transfer zipped data archives.

Detail Purpose HOSTNAME, USERNAME, PASSWORD Credentials for the FTP transfer. Project Folder Select the project folder first. Study Folder Select the correct study folder before uploading files.

docs.title: FileZilla Procedure
docs.text:
1. Open FileZilla or another FTP client.
  2. Enter the host, username, and password from the portal.
  3. Navigate to the project folder.
  4. Open the correct study folder.
  5. Upload all zipped raw/derived data files.

docs.title: Map Uploaded Files
docs.text:
Mapping links the FTP-transferred files to the sample and assay metadata.

Mapping Field What to Select or Enter Study ID Study under which the file was uploaded. Uploaded File Exact file transferred through FTP. Sample ID Correct IMDA sample ID connected to that file. Protocol / Assay Analytical method or assay used to generate the file. MD5 Checksum Lowercase checksum value generated before upload.
  1. Open Map Uploaded Files from the IMDA sidebar.
  2. Verify that all uploaded files appear under the correct Study ID.
  3. Link each file to the correct sample ID and protocol.
  4. Enter the matching MD5 checksum.
  5. Confirm every sample has its corresponding raw and/or processed data file.
  6. Click Validate All Files For This Study only after checking all metadata and file mappings.

Final Submission Control

After final validation, direct edit options for project, study, and sample metadata may disappear. Check all details before clicking the final validation button.

docs.title: MD5 Checksum
docs.text:
Generate checksums before transferring data files. The MD5 checksum confirms that the uploaded file is identical to the local source file.

Access the Tool: IMDA MD5 Checksum Tool.

docs.title: What to Prepare
docs.text: File Type What to Prepare Rule Raw data file Instrument output from MS or NMR. Compress complex folders into ZIP files before upload. Derived data file Processed output generated from raw data. Keep names consistent with the experiment template. Metadata template Sample and experiment spreadsheets. File names in templates must match uploaded files exactly. Checksum file md5sum.txt generated by the IMDA script. Use the checksum matching each uploaded file.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Download the script for Windows, macOS, or Linux.
  2. Run the script in the directory containing the raw data files.
  3. Confirm that the script generates md5sum.txt.
  4. Use the checksum values from md5sum.txt during file mapping.

Checksum Rules

Enter MD5 checksum values in lowercase and make sure each checksum corresponds to the exact ZIP file uploaded.

docs.title: Reviewer Access URL
docs.text:
Use the reviewer access URL to share private study records with journal reviewers or collaborators.

Action: Open the submitted study details and locate URLs to Share Study Records.

docs.title: What to Check Before Sharing
docs.text: Item Check Study record Confirm that the correct study is selected. Metadata Check project, study, sample, assay, and file details. Uploaded files Confirm that raw and processed files are mapped correctly. Reviewer URL Copy the activated URL from the portal.

docs.title: Security Rate-Limit Policy
docs.text:
• Only 5 unique individuals can access the shared link within a 24-hour period.
  • If the limit is reached, additional users must wait until the 24-hour window resets.

docs.title: Generate the Secure Link
docs.text:
1. Click Activate Link.
  2. Use Copy to copy the URL.
  3. Share the URL with the journal editor or reviewer.

docs.title: Sample
docs.text: Sample registration defines the origin, source, classification, and file count for all samples.

docs.title: What to Fill
docs.text: Field What to Enter Writing Guideline Select Study* Study ID to which these samples belong. Choose the correct study before uploading the template. Source* Biological source, such as organism part, tissue, cell line, biofluid, or culture. Prefer controlled vocabulary terms; avoid local abbreviations. Organism Name* Scientific organism name. Use binomial name, for example Homo sapiens or Oryza sativa. Taxonomy ID* NCBI taxonomy identifier fetched by the system. Cross-check that the ID matches the organism name. Sample File Template* Completed sample metadata spreadsheet. Do not change template headers.

docs.title: Template Requirements
docs.text:
Template Column What to Fill Sample Name / Sample Label Unique sample name used by the submitter. It should match the naming used in experiment metadata. Organism / Source Details Biological source, organism part, disease/condition, treatment, or cell type where applicable. Number of files per sample Exact count of raw or derived files linked to that sample. Replicate / Group Information Biological group, treatment group, control group, or replicate number where requested. Missing or Not Applicable Values Enter NA instead of leaving required cells blank.

After template submission, IMDA generates sample IDs. Use those IDs in the experiment template.

Final Action:

  1. Download and complete the sample file template.
  2. Upload it using Choose File.
  3. Click Submit to register sample metadata.

docs.title: Study
docs.text:
Study registration defines the scientific context and experimental design. The study is linked to the registered project.

Workflow Action: Select the relevant Project ID, then complete the Study Details and Author List sections.

docs.title: Study Details
docs.text: Field What to Enter Writing Guideline Title* Specific title of the experiment or dataset. Use a precise title that includes organism, sample type, and assay where possible. Study Type* Analytical technology used, such as Mass Spectrometry (MS) or Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR). Select the closest available portal option. Data Type / Summary Targeted, semi-targeted, or untargeted metabolomics scope and a short study summary. Use 3-5 sentences; avoid manuscript-length background. Release Date* Date on which the data can become publicly available. Use the required portal date format. Publication / Approval DOI, PubMed ID, manuscript status, IEC/IBSC approval, or institutional approval number. Enter official identifiers exactly as issued.

docs.title: Author List
docs.text:
Click Add Author to include all contributors. Check names, emails, and affiliations because these details support final attribution.

Field What to Enter Name Full contributor name as it should appear in attribution. Email Active institutional or professional email address. Affiliation Department, institute, city, and country where requested. Role PI, submitter, author, curator contact, or other available role.

Final Action: Click Submit. The portal assigns a study accession or study identifier such as IMS_xxxxxx.

docs.title: Submitted Data
docs.text: Use Submitted Data to monitor submitted studies and curation progress.

docs.title: Tracking Your Study
docs.text:
1. Review the table for Project ID, Study ID, Study Title, and Date of Submission.
  2. Open the Study ID or row details to view full metadata and current status.
  3. Use the final IMP_xxxxxx and IMS_xxxxxx accession identifiers for citation after release.
Status Meaning Action Required Submitted Initial state awaiting review. None unless IMDA contacts you. In Curation Curator is reviewing metadata and data files. Check registered email frequently. Public Study is released for download. Cite the final accession identifiers.

Processing Timeline

The testing portal states that submissions are processed within 7 days, and submitters are notified by email.

docs.title: Corrections After Submission
docs.text:
Use Edit File Data only when metadata or file corrections are required before final validation or during curator-requested correction.

Submission Status Edit Button Status Required Action Pre-Submission Active Click the edit option for the relevant row. Post-Submission Disabled or hidden Contact IMDA support to request temporary edit access.

Common edit actions include:

  • Edit Project / Study / Sample Details: Correct metadata before final validation.
  • Edit Upload Run: Replace corrupted or incorrect raw data files.
  • Edit Metabolite / Compound File: Replace the processed metabolite summary file.

docs.title: Controlled Vocabulary Updates
docs.text: Use Browse Lists to check whether an organism, source, or MS/NMR instrument term already exists. If the required term is missing, use Update List to submit a new controlled vocabulary request.

docs.title: Support and Citation
docs.text: Item Guidance Repository Indian Metabolome Data Archive (IMDA) of the Indian Biological Data Centre (IBDC). Project Accession Use the assigned IMP_xxxxxx identifier. Study Accession Use the assigned IMS_xxxxxx identifier. Support Email Contact imdasupport@ibdc.rcb.res.in for assistance.
